thread:
Maria G.: Quick question — we need to decide acceptable timing tolerances for fallback from Dedicated -> Hosted when eviction/burst hits. Current naive is immediate fallback; ops says that's noisy. Thoughts?
Sam K.: Immediate fallback causes double work (client retries + new model spin). Can we do a 2-tier grace: 3s fast failover vs 30s buffered fallback?
Anya L.: What do you mean by buffered? Hold requests in queue on edge? That increases latency tail.
Sam K.: Buffered = short local stall with best-effort batching + probe to hosted. If hosted responds within TTL then we switch, otherwise return error. TTL could be 5-15s. Reduces churn.
Devon (infra): We must consider token accounting and billing when we buffer. Also security: requests touching hosted may need redaction for private deployments.
Maria G.: Right. Also customers expect SLA continuity for Dedicated. Proposal: config knobs per tenant: fallback_policy: { probe_interval, probe_ttl, max_buffer_ms, degrade_mode } — defaults: 100ms probe_interval, 5000ms probe_ttl, 200ms max_buffer, degrade_mode=redirect.
Sam K.: Those defaults seem aggressive. 100ms probe interval might overwhelm control plane during widespread evictions.
Anya L.: Suggest probe backoff: exponential from 100ms to 2s over 5 attempts.
Devon (infra): +1 for backoff. Also add a 'sensitive' flag that prevents fallback to hosted for tenants with private data. Should surface early.
Maria G.: Agreed. Draft config snippet:
```
fallback_policy:
  probe_interval_ms: 200
  probe_ttl_ms: 7000
  max_buffer_ms: 250
  backoff: [200, 400, 800, 1600]
  sensitive: false
  audit_sink: redis://audit.internal
```
Anya L.: How do we route partial responses? e.g., if KV cache present we might return cached prefix and then fallback stream.
Sam K.: Proposal: keep deterministic contract: if fallback happens mid-stream we send final token chunk with meta {fallback:true, origin:hosted} so clients can reconcile.
Devon (infra): Need to update runtime handshake: new field 'fallback_allowed' + 'audit_tag'.
deploy-bot: deploy-checker: runtime schema bump required in 1 microservice (adapters) — rolling deploy recommended.
Devon (infra): I'll open a tiny RFC + rollout plan. Anyone opposed to defaults above?
Anya L.: No objections. Can we add a metric: fallback_latency_p95 and fallback_success_rate?
Maria G.: yes. I'll file follow-up and tag infra/product.
deploy-bot: Added task INF-1245 to infra board: 'Fallback timing & SLA concessions' — https://boards.redwood/INF-1245 :thumbsup:
Maria G.: Thanks all.
